title: What I want vs What I get
author: Puzzleheaded_Math_55
selftext:
[What I want](https://preview.redd.it/r17fq5cwywef1.png?width=1536&format=png&auto=webp&s=e579f6b499d9aaba1f260062ad14308e876769ae)

[What I get](https://preview.redd.it/ppz0wwa3zwef1.png?width=830&format=png&auto=webp&s=ad5d906981c51f99195576a447bbb59fbb1f85b6)

I tried both ChatGPT and Claude, no LLMs can create a Mitochondria maze. Most of the time, the mazes they created and worked are too generic. How may I improve?

comments.author: PikachuDash
comments.body: In the "What I get" screenshot it doesn't look like a maze at all? I would guess that the AI focuses too much on the "mitochondria" part instead of the actual maze. So I would try to instruct it to focus on creating a good, non-generic maze game and then taking care of theming it as mitochondria only when that is working well.

replies.author: Puzzleheaded_Math_55
replies.body:
https://preview.redd.it/alyz26co11ff1.png?width=1022&format=png&auto=webp&s=f3f619b96e914f4c19f2adfd88ed0ed169722a7b

Yes, agree. Both Claude and GPT can create playable mazes as shown, however, if I push a little bit on the mitochondria, they start to be clueless.

replies.author: PikachuDash
replies.body:
When the maze is working gameplay wise, maybe just tell it to adopt the style and color palette of your "what I want" screenshot without mentioning mitochondria at all. If that's what is confusing the AI.

Using lines instead of blocks for the borders and getting the maze in an oval shape should go a long way towards your goal and the AI should totally be capable of that.

replies.author: Puzzleheaded_Math_55
replies.body:
https://preview.redd.it/en6lpciv41ff1.png?width=1912&format=png&auto=webp&s=d99d5eb5bc98916b711174893bdc8b5f5c76f373

This is one of the outputs from gpt4.1 for a 2D maze. It gets the color and bean-shape as my input, but still has trouble to align on details.
